title: Women Will Get 33% Reservation, Congress Cannot Stop It, Amit Shah Says
excerpt: Speaking on Constitution Day, the Home Minister blamed the Congress for blocking the amendments needed to operationalise the 2023 women's quota law. The Congress says it backed the law and wants it implemented immediately.
body:
• Home Minister Amit Shah said on Constitution Day that women will definitely get 33 per cent reservation in Parliament and state assemblies, and that the Congress cannot stop it.
  • The quota is already law under the 106th Constitutional Amendment of 2023, but its rollout is tied to a fresh delimitation and seat expansion; an enabling bill failed to win the required two-thirds majority in April 2026.
  • The Congress says it supported the 2023 Act and wants the quota implemented immediately, without waiting for delimitation; P. Chidambaram accused Shah of being "economical with the truth."
  • Parliament reconvenes on November 30, when the government is expected to push the pending delimitation-linked bills again.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared on Thursday that women in India will definitely receive 33 per cent reservation in Parliament and state legislative assemblies, accusing the Congress and other opposition parties of obstructing the constitutional amendments needed to put the quota into force.

Speaking at a Samvidhan Gaurav Divas event in New Delhi to mark Constitution Day, Shah directed his remarks at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. "The constitutional amendment providing 33 per cent reservation to women in Parliament and State Assemblies — the Congress party has been sitting on it and blocking it. Today, I want to tell Rahul ji: it is the resolve of the Bharatiya Janata Party and our leader Narendra Modi that the women of this country will definitely get 33 per cent reservation; you cannot stop us," he said, according to ANI. Shah also said the BJP would implement the Uniform Civil Code in BJP-ruled states.

"It is the resolve of the Bharatiya Janata Party and our leader Narendra Modi that the women of this country will definitely get 33 per cent reservation; you cannot stop us."

— Amit Shah, Union Home Minister

A law passed in 2023, still not in force

The reservation itself is already on the statute book. The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, enacted as the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 after being introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill, reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies and the Delhi assembly. The dispute is over timing and mechanism: the government has linked the rollout to a fresh delimitation exercise and an expansion of seats, and an earlier enabling constitutional amendment bill failed to secure the mandatory two-thirds majority in Parliament in April 2026. The government's proposal would raise the Lok Sabha to 850 seats, with about 283 of them reserved for women on rotation.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=E8D6DuxUlaA

The opposition's answer

The Congress-led opposition contests the government's account. It argues the 33 per cent reservation can and should be implemented immediately, within the existing strength of Parliament and the assemblies, without waiting for delimitation, and alleges that linking the quota to constituency redrawing is a political strategy to reshape electoral boundaries in the ruling party's favour. On Friday, Congress leader P. Chidambaram accused Shah of misrepresenting his party's position: "Home Minister Amit Shah either has amnesia or is economical with the truth," he wrote, noting that the 106th Amendment was passed by both Houses on September 20 and 21, 2023, that Congress fully supported its passage, and that it has been demanding the Act's immediate implementation. He questioned the need for a new women's reservation bill at all.

What happens next

Parliament is scheduled to reconvene on November 30, 2026, with the Lok Sabha sitting that day and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, and the government is preparing to push once again for the pending bills tied to the quota's rollout. The arithmetic is the obstacle: a constitutional amendment needs around 360 votes in the Lok Sabha, while the BJP-led NDA is reported to count 319 members for sure, 241 of them from the BJP. Whether the quota reaches the statute's promise in this session depends on votes the government does not yet publicly have.
